pr_title: caddytls: keep repeated matchers in nested matcher sets
pr_body:
`caddytls.ParseCaddyfileNestedMatcherSet` groups the tokens of a repeated matcher, then hands them to `caddyfile.UnmarshalModule`, which reads only the first segment. So this block

```
match {
	sni example.com
	sni example.net
}
```

gives `{"sni":["example.com"]}`, and the second line is ignored without an error. A `remote_ip !10.1.2.3` exclusion on its own line is lost the same way.

This passes all the tokens to `UnmarshalCaddyfile`, like `caddyhttp.ParseCaddyfileNestedMatcherSet` does. The TLS matchers are written to handle several segments. A repeated `sni_regexp` now returns its existing "regular expression can only be used once" error instead of dropping the second pattern.

It came up while working on #8097. I kept it out of the `not` matcher PR, as asked there.

## Assistance Disclosure

Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) found this while testing the `not` matcher, wrote the fix, I tested it. I reviewed every line
